extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of aesthetics and Kantian philosophy (readers studying the Critique of Judgment)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of Kant's criteria for judging the sublime (mathematical and dynamical) and its distinction from the beautiful; explains the mental faculties involved, the affective quality of the judgement, and conditions for its universality. Intended to guide how to recognize, describe, and justify aesthetic judgements about sublime natural phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterested pleasure / subjective purposiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything which is to give disinterested pleasure to the merely reflective Judgement must bring with the representation of it, subjective and, as subjective, universally valid purposiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correct aesthetic judgement should be made disinterestedly (without personal interest) and register a subjective purposiveness that the judge treats as universally valid. This is the formal condition for an aesthetic appraisal separate from cognitive or practical determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Beautiful: purposiveness of form and pleasure apart from interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Beautiful is what pleases in the mere judgement (and therefore not by the medium of sensation in accordance with a concept of the Understanding). It must please apart from all interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To judge something as beautiful, the representation should manifest formal purposiveness and a harmonious free play of Imagination and Understanding. The pleasure is positive, restful contemplation, and ought not to be grounded in desire or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sublime: opposition to sensible interest and reference to Reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sublime is what pleases immediately through its opposition to the interest of sense...the representation of which determines the mind to think the unattainability of nature regarded as a presentation of Ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime judgements arise when sensible interest is thwarted (e.g., imagination fails to comprehend) and the mind is forced to appeal to Reason and Ideas. The judgement's focus is the subject's response (relation to supersensible Ideas), not objective properties alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sublime (magnitude/inadequacy of imagination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aesthetical estimation of magnitude in which the Imagination's effort towards comprehension surpasses its power to grasp the progressive apprehension (the Imagination is inadequate for the presentation of the concept of magnitude).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When magnitude (size, infinity) strains the Imagination beyond its capacity for a single intuition, the judgement is mathematically sublime. Evidence: apprehension of enormous units (earth, stellar systems) that force reference to Reason/Ideas rather than complete sensory comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monstrous vs Colossal distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: An object is monstrous if by its size it destroys the purpose which constitutes the concept of it. But the mere presentation of a concept is called colossal, which is almost too great for any presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether size undermines the object's defining purpose (monstrous) or simply overwhelms presentation without destroying the concept (colossal). This distinction helps classify extreme magnitudes when judging the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamical Sublime (nature as might provoking awe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature regarded in an aesthetical judgement as might that has no dominion over us is dynamically sublime. If nature excites fear (but observed in security), it can be judged dynamically sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dynamical sublimity arises from perceived might/resistance (storms, volcanoes, oceans) that would overwhelm our faculties; experienced from safety it raises energies and reveals a non-sensuous standard of superiority in our Reason. Key condition: excitation of fear conceived without actual danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublimity resides in the subject, not the object
rubrics_metrics.description: True sublimity must be sought only in the mind of the [subject] judging, not in the natural Object, the judgement upon which occasions this state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing sublimity, focus on the subject's mental state (imagination, reason, feeling of destiny) rather than treating sublimity as an intrinsic property of natural objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affective quality of the sublime: mixed pain and pleasure — respect
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of our incapacity to attain to an Idea...is RESPECT. The feeling of the Sublime is therefore a feeling of pain, arising from the want of accordance between the aesthetical estimation of magnitude formed by the Imagination and the estimation of the same formed by Reason; there is at the same time a pleasure arising from correspondence with rational Ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the characteristic affect: an initial painful sense of inadequacy combined with a higher pleasure (respect) when this inadequacy points to our supersensible destination. Describe both elements when justifying a sublime judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movement vs rest: Imagination–Reason conflict vs harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: In judging the Beautiful, Imagination and Understanding generate a subjective purposiveness by means of their harmony (restful contemplation). In judging the Sublime, Imagination and Reason generate a subjective purposiveness by means of their conflict (movement, vibration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which faculties are engaged: beauty = harmonious play (Imagination + Understanding); sublime = productive conflict (Imagination stretched, Reason invoked). The phenomenology (rest vs movement) should be part of the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of a moral susceptibility / culture for judging the sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: That the mind be attuned to feel the sublime postulates a susceptibility of the mind for Ideas...without development of moral Ideas, that which we call sublime presents itself to the uneducated man merely as terrible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A credible claim of sublimity presumes some cultivation or moral sensibility: the judge must be disposed to regard the Imagination's strain as teleologically connected to Reason/Ideas. This explains intersubjective divergence: less-cultured observers may only feel terror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity / a priori claim of aesthetic judgements about the sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: In this modality of aesthetical judgements...we ascribe necessity to this aesthetical judgement...it enables us to recognise in them an a priori principle...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting a judgement of sublimity, the form of the judgement claims universal assent grounded in a priori principles (via the presupposed moral feeling). Evaluations should note this claim of necessity and its basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative vs Positive satisfaction (beautiful vs sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: The satisfaction in the Sublime of nature is then only negative (whilst that in the Beautiful is positive); viz. a feeling that the Imagination is depriving itself of its freedom, while it is purposively determined according to a different law from that of its empirical employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the experienced satisfaction: beauty produces positive, affirmative pleasure; sublime produces a negative pleasure (pleasure through negation of sensuous freedom) tied to moral/ideal reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime as presentation of ideas via the failure of sensuous presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The effort — and the feeling of the unattainability of the Idea by means of the Imagination — is itself a presentation of the subjective purposiveness of our mind in the employment of the Imagination for its supersensible destination; and forces us, subjectively, to think nature itself in its totality as a presentation of something supersensible, without being able objectively to arrive at this presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judgement of the sublime should show how the Imagination's failure functions hermeneutically: the breakdown is evidence of access to Ideas (supersensible substratum). Explanations should trace how sensuous inadequacy leads to Idea-positing by Reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and conditions for pleasurable sublime experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Bold, overhanging, and as it were threatening, rocks; clouds piled up in the sky, moving with lightning flashes and thunder peals; volcanoes...hurricanes...the boundless ocean...the lofty waterfall...these exhibit our faculty of resistance as insignificantly small...The sight of them is the more attractive, the more fearful it is, provided only that we are in security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples (mountains, storms, ocean, waterfalls) to justify sublime judgements and note the crucial condition: the observer must be in safety. If fear is real and present, pleasure/sublimity is precluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to religion, humility, and distinction from superstition
rubrics_metrics.description: Only if he is conscious of an upright disposition pleasing to God do those operations of might serve to awaken in him the Idea of the sublimity of this Being...In this way religion is essentially distinguished from superstition. The latter establishes...fear and apprehension...without according Him any high esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relating sublimity to religious phenomena, distinguish reverence (sublime response grounded in moral consciousness) from mere superstition (fear without esteem). This criterion guides interpretation of religious awe as sublime vs fearful subjection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification framework: pleasant / beautiful / sublime / absolutely good
rubrics_metrics.description: In reference to the feeling of pleasure an object is to be classified as either pleasant, or beautiful, or sublime, or good (absolutely)...The pleasant is motive of desire and reducible to quantity; the beautiful requires representation of a certain quality; the sublime consists in the relation by which the sensible in the representation of nature is judged available for a possible supersensible use; the absolutely good is determined by a priori moral concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this taxonomy when evaluating aesthetic responses: determine whether the response is merely pleasant (quantitative), beautiful (formal quality), sublime (relation to supersensible Ideas), or absolutely good (moral necessity). Use the distinctions to justify category assignments.
